items.title: 52043_Herman Autrey oral history interview
items.q: The name 'Tom' is mentioned repeatedly in the context of Fats Waller's behavior ('Now, Tom. Now, Tom.') and as someone Fats calls for ('call Hermie, get Hermie, I want Hermie. Now Tom, uh, it's no use you worrying about that now.'), but the interviewee (Herman Autrey) does not describe a direct pers

ctx.x: Well this -- of course one of the incredible things, I think, about the Fats Waller recordings, all through that period, is that he had so many awful tunes in there, terrible.

That we did, and he threatened, he's hit the piano, I won't do it! I won't do it! So the manager would come out. Now, Tom. Now, Tom. Especially Kirkpeby. Now Tom. And Thomas, now after all, but -- now, I -- for me. I think you should, and they would go through this business, you know. And he would say well, maybe so, all right, but he was --
Now for instance, I remember one tune, 'Annie Don't Live Here No More.'
